newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 23.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Co, which is responsible for its contents.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- B.A.T INDUSTRIES COSTS TOBACCO DEAL

B.A.T Industries is facing a one-off payment of $1.7 billion and a rising scale of annual payments over 25 years following the settlement between the US tobacco industry and the country's state governments. The annual payments will start at $1.4 billion - based on B.A.T's 16.5 percent share of the US market - and rise to $15 billion in the fifth year.
-- SURVEY'S NEW IMAGE OF BRITISH SHOPWORKERS

A survey published Monday by the London Chamber of Commerce and Industry reveals that most of Britain's shopworkers are well-educated, highly-paid professionals. The report details the results of a study carried out with the University of Westminster which compared the working conditions for shopworkers around the country with those in the capital.
-- BAKERY SERVICES GROUP TO SELL 49 PERCENT SLICE IN 2.2 MLN STG AIM FLOAT

Bakery Services has revealed plans to float on the Alternative Investment Market in a placement which is expected to value the company at 2.2 million stg. The company, which runs bakeries for supermarket groups, said the float would 'help raise the profile of the group, strengthening the company's plans for growth'.
THE TIMES -- CWC ESCALATES PHONE TARIFF WAR

Cable and telecoms group CWC has initiated a new telecommunications price war with the launch of a new tariff which aims to take business customers from British Telecom. The new CWC tariff undercuts BT by between 39 percent and 48 percent in areas covered by the four cable groups - Nynex, Bell Cablemedia, Mercury and Videotron.
-- THOMSON TO SELL TRAVEL BUSINESS

Canadian publisher Thomson Corporation is in talks with City investment banks ahead of a trade sale of its UK-based tour operator Thomson. Prospective buyers for the business - which comprises Thomson Holidays, Lunn Poly and Britannia Airways - include British Airways, Carlson Travel and German tour operator Touristik Union International. The Thomson Corporation is seeking to raise funds for its strategy of concentrating on its core information and publishing business.
-- SAINSBURY STORE ADDS A SURGERY

Supermarket chain Sainsbury is to trial its first walk-in private medical centre at a Sheffield store due to be opened in October. The surgery will be sited beside the group's largest store in Sheffield, and will house four doctors. It will be operated by Sinclair Montrose Healthcare, which will rent the land from Sainsbury's.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BANKING RIVALS MAY MERGE

Barclays Bank is contemplating a takeover bid or a merger with High Street rival National Westmister Bank, according to reports. The reports follow a profit warning last week from NatWest and come amid growing concern among major shareholders with the performance of the group.
-- AUSTRALIA BUYS 400 MLN STG-WORTH OF HAWK PLANES

The Australian government has placed an order for 12 Hawk planes with British Aerospace, a contract worth more than 400 million stg which will help secure jobs at BAe's factories at Warton, Lancashire, and Brough, East Yorkshire. Confirmation of the deal was given by Australian prime minister John Howard during a visit to the Brough factory on Sunday.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SHAKE-UP FOR PRIVATE FINANCE INITIATIVE

The government is expected on Monday to abolish the Private Finance Panel as part of an overhaul of the way public projects are funded through the Private Finance Initiative (PFI). The changes, which are also likely to include a reorganisation of the Private Finance Executive and a strengthening of the private finance units operating within individual government departments, follow a month-long review of the PFI.
-- NORTHERN ELECTRIC AND CALORTEX IN ALLIANCE TALKS

US-owned regional electricity company Northern Electric has held talks with independent gas supplier Calortex over a possible energy alliance. Calor Group has put up for sale its 50 percent stake in Calortex, and is believed to have held talks with at least three regional electricity companies, with Northern Electric thought to be the main bidder.
-- DEPARTMENT STORE SALES UP 10 PERCENT

A report from Corporate Intelligence on Retailing has claimed that the department store sector is one of the fastest-growing retail markets in the UK. The report reveals that the top 50 department store groups increased their sales by 5.7 percent to 5.2 billion stg in 1995-96, and estimates the increase for 1996-97 will be almost 10 percent.
